svg.text: Domains and DNS: the internet's phone book
Concept 5 · the name yourname.my.id is rented at a registrar, its records are kept at Cloudflare
a verified email; an ID card if asked
from then on, every record of
this name is written at Cloudflare
your VPS IP (203.0.113.10 = example); a small TTL
(300 s) while setting up; no AAAA record
A phone asks: where is iot.yourname.my.id?
Then the phone connects straight to 203.0.113.10:443. The resolver remembers the answer for TTL seconds; check from the laptop: nslookup iot.yourname.my.id 1.1.1.1
The author's lab: a stand-in DNS in Docker (pebble-challtestsrv), not Cloudflare.
the answer = your VPS's real IP
visitors connect STRAIGHT to the VPS:
REQUIRED for mqtt.; on the main path iot. too
the answer = Cloudflare's IP, not the VPS
other ports: Spectrum, Enterprise plan only
The free path: a record for the tunnel
Add route → Published application, Service URL http://web:80)
check in the DNS list that this CNAME exists; no mqtt
record: the broker is only on the home network
.my.id is on the Public Suffix List: yourname.my.id counts
as your own domain, so Let's Encrypt's limit
(50 new certificates per week) isn't shared with others.
Honestly: the registrar and Cloudflare steps come from
the docs; the author has no account. Support for a .my.id
zone on Cloudflare's free plan isn't checked yet; if refused:
the main path uses the registrar's DNS, the free path needs another domain.
